title: Leadership, autonomy, and how we work together
vimeoName: Module 12 - Leadership, autonomy, and how we work together

segments.text: Last module, and I've saved the most important conversation
for the end, how we work together.
Not the org chart, the real thing.
What I believe about leading people,
what I expect from you,
and what you have every right to expect from me.
Let me start with a confession.
Nobody taught me hospitality management.
I was a lawyer who fell in love
with the field of carnations.
Almost everything I know about running this place,
I learned by doing it, and by getting it wrong first.
So when I talk about mistakes,
I'm not being generous from some throne of perfection.
I'm speaking as this company's most experienced maker
of mistakes.
Here's my first principle.
I'd rather correct your decision
than make all the decisions.
You are the person on the ground,
in front of the guest with the pan on the fire,
with the room to prepare.
You see things I will never see from Lisbon
or from a spreadsheet.
If you wait for permission for every judgment call,
we become slow and worse.
You stop thinking, because why think
when someone above you does it for you?
So the rule is, when the guest is in front of you
and something needs solving, solve it.
Use the values as your compass.
The long game, the relationship,
the coherence between what we say and what we do.
If your solution costs a bottle of wine
or a free dessert to save a guest's evening, do it.
Tell your manager after.
I will never, ever punish someone
for a generous decision made in good faith for a guest.
Never.
Second principle, the mistake is not the problem.
I think it is.
In eight years of building and eight more of operating,
I've seen every kind of mistake.
Doubles booked, dishes burned, reservations lost,
pipes opened at the wrong moment.
Here's what I know.
A mistake caught early is an anecdote.
A mistake hidden is a crisis.
So the deal between us is this.
You bring me the problem while it's small
and I bring you calm, help and zero drama.
You hide it until it explodes
and then we have two problems.
And the second one is trust.
Speak early, always.
This applies upward too, by the way.
When I'm wrong, tell me.
I promise you it won't be career limiting.
The people who've challenged me best
are the people I trust most today.
Third, standards are how we respect each other.
I ask a lot, you know this, the details,
the coherence, the promise keeping.
Model six wasn't gentle, but understand why.
High standards are a form of respect.
Respect for the guest who paid us their trust.
Respect for the colleague whose work or work
either lifts or undermines.
Because in a place like this, everything touches everything.
A light room delays a check-in, delays dinner,
sours an evening.
And respect for yourself.
Nobody feels proud going home from sloppy work.
And pride in work is one of the great pleasures of life.
I want Kravero to be the hardest job some of you ever love.
Force.
We grow people, not just vegetables.
The regeneration we preach for soil applies to careers.
I want people from Sao Teotonio and Odemira
to build real professional lives here
without leaving their land.
That's social sustainability with names and faces.
If you want to learn another section, another skill,
wine, English, numbers, say so.
The person cleaning houses today
can be running housekeeping in three years.
Versions of that sentence have already come through
here more than once.
My commitment, we will always prefer to promote from within.
And your ambition is welcome here.
What I ask in return is that you teach others what you learn.
Knowledge that stays in one head is knowledge
the team doesn't have.
Fifth, and this one goes both directions.
Well-being is non-negotiable.
I set it in the values module and I'll close with it.
This industry has a long, ugly tradition
of burning people out and calling it passion.
Not here, not on my watch.
Breaks are real, days off are real, the schedule is human.
And if it ever isn't, escalate it to me if needed.
I would rather run at slightly lower capacity
than run on exhausted people.
Because exhausted people can't give warms.
And warms is our entire product.
And between yourselves, watch out for each other.
Cover for the colleague having a hard week.
They'll cover you in yours.
The team is the first community we regenerate.
Let me land this whole thing.
16 years ago, there was a field of carnations
and a lawyer with a dream that most sensible people found
ridiculous.
Today, there are 38 houses full of stories,
a farm that feeds hundreds of people a week,
a beach bar on the sand, a table inside a museum in Lisbon,
weddings under our pines, and a team,
you that carries all of it.
None of it was inevitable.
All of it came from believing that the place well cared for
cares for those who inhabited.
And then working season after season as if that were true.
It turned out it was.
You are part of that now, not employed by it, part of it.
And my deepest hope for your time here
is the same thing we promised the guests
because it turns out the brand was never just for them.
FICA pretends, stay, belong.
Thank you for listening to all of this.
Now, let's get to work.
